name: diagram
purpose: A node-and-connector diagram for marketing pages: the request path of an architecture, a routing policy, a product's place in the platform. The consumer names one of the official diagrams with `name` — the closed library of 28 drawings in webkit's assets, one starter architecture per Azion product plus the page diagrams the product pages tab through — or passes a one-off `spec`: the nodes, how they are arranged, and the edges between them. The component lays the nodes out with real CSS (rows, branches, grids and framed groups), then measures the laid-out nodes and draws every connector, port and edge label on top. Nothing is drawn on a fixed canvas: the layout reflows below its container breakpoint into a stacked column — centred on one axis, or an indented tree where the row branches — and the connectors are re-measured, so a diagram stays legible from a phone to a wide band.
useWhen: Showing how a request travels through Azion — client, application, the product the page is about, and its outcomes.
Showing a routing or failover policy as nodes and labelled edges, with the path a request takes highlighted.
Filling the media cell of a marketing band (`media-tabs`, `media-split`) with an architecture instead of a picture.
avoidWhen: For a world map of points of presence → use `network-map`.
For a sequence of steps the reader follows in order → use `stepper` or an ordered list.
For live data or anything the reader operates — a diagram is a figure, not a control.
related: illustration` — the drawn scene library; a diagram is generated from data, an illustration is authored art. Both pick an official drawing by `name`.
media-tabs` — hosts one diagram per tab in its media column; key each `Diagram` by its tab so it re-measures.
frame-box` — the registration frame a diagram's groups and tiles are drawn in.
tag` — the status chip a card or item node carries.
bestPractices: Keep a diagram to about four columns in the wide layout so it fits a band's media cell; split a larger story into several diagrams.
Light exactly one node with `lit` — the product the diagram is about — and mark the request path with `active` on its nodes and edges.
Use `gap: 'wide'` on a row whose edges carry labels, so the chips have room between the nodes.
Name an official diagram instead of rebuilding its `spec`, so the same architecture is the same drawing on every page. Reach for `spec` only for a diagram the library does not have.

Every named diagram carries its own one-sentence description. Give a `spec` diagram an `ariaLabel` (in the prop or in the spec) that states what it shows; the drawing itself is hidden from assistive technology.

Do: for a vertical flow in a docs column (a command → the CLI → the API → the resources), use one `row`. In the column it stacks centred, every connector runs through the horizontal centre of both nodes and an edge label sits centred on its line.
Don't: nudge nodes or labels with wrappers, margins or spacer nodes to centre a flow; the layout does it.
Reach for `card` for platform pieces, `item` for models and providers, `pill` for a client, `tile` for an icon-only grid cell, and `app` for the consumer's own application.

props.name: name
props.doc: Name of an official diagram in the asset library; ignored when spec is set.

props.name: spec
props.doc: The nodes, their layout and the edges between them, for a diagram the library does not have.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible description of the whole diagram; empty uses the description the spec carries.

examples.name: Spec
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import Diagram from '@aziontech/webkit/diagram'

  const spec = {
    nodes: [
      {
        key: 'user',
        kind: 'pill',
        title: 'User',
        icon: 'pi pi-user',
        active: true
      },
      {
        key: 'routing',
        kind: 'card',
        eyebrow: 'Routing',
        title: 'Nearest data center',
        icon: 'pi pi-directions',
        active: true
      },
      {
        key: 'workload',
        kind: 'card',
        eyebrow: 'Workload',
        title: 'shop.example.com',
        icon: 'ai ai-workloads',
        status: {
          label: 'Live',
          severity: 'success'
        },
        active: true,
        lit: true
      },
      {
        key: 'cache',
        kind: 'item',
        eyebrow: 'Cache',
        title: 'Served from cache',
        icon: 'ai ai-tiered-cache',
        active: true
      },
      {
        key: 'origin',
        kind: 'item',
        eyebrow: 'Origin',
        title: 'origin.example.com',
        icon: 'pi pi-database'
      }
    ],
    layout: {
      gap: 'wide',
      row: [
        {
          node: 'user'
        },
        {
          node: 'routing'
        },
        {
          node: 'workload'
        },
        {
          branches: [
            {
              node: 'cache'
            },
            {
              node: 'origin'
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    edges: [
      {
        from: 'user',
        to: 'routing',
        active: true
      },
      {
        from: 'routing',
        to: 'workload',
        active: true
      },
      {
        from: 'workload',
        to: 'cache',
        label: 'hit',
        active: true
      },
      {
        from: 'workload',
        to: 'origin',
        label: 'miss'
      }
    ]
  }
</script>

<template>
  <Diagram
    :spec="spec"
    aria-label="A user request is routed to the nearest data center and reaches the workload, which serves it from cache on a hit and from the origin on a miss."
  />
</template>

        kind: 'card',
        eyebrow: 'AI Gateway',
        title: 'Route by cost',
        icon: 'ai ai-gateway',
        status: {
          label: 'On',
          severity: 'success'
        },
        active: true,
        lit: true
      },
      {
        key: 'model',
        kind: 'item',

      }
    ],

        {
          node: 'app'
        },
        {

        },
        {

              node: 'model'
            },
            {
              node: 'cache'
            }
          ]
